explanation: Jurassic Park's raptors were far bigger, closer in size to relatives such as Deinonychus. The real animal was feathered: its forearm bones carry quill knobs, where wing feathers were anchored.

claims.text: Velociraptor was about the size of a turkey.
Velociraptor was much smaller than an adult human, a horse or a lion.
The raptors in Jurassic Park were much bigger than Velociraptor, closer in size to relatives such as Deinonychus.
Velociraptor forearm fossils show quill knobs, where feathers were anchored.

writerNotes: Self-check (guide 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: four listed; high: c1 (checker_doubt, standing in for counterintuitive, which the tooling's riskReason enum lacks; C26 makes the key of a counterintuitive item high); standard: c2, c3 and c4. datasets: no pinned dataset in content/datasets/manifest.json covers animal or plant biology (it holds countries, languages, currencies, cities, elements, Nobel Prizes, Olympic Games, World Cups, art collections and Natural Earth), so none applies, and the high-risk claims need web evidence from checker A; one search on Velociraptor size and quill knobs should cover c1, c3 and c4. rivalTest: Argued for 'An adult human', the size the films made famous: that is the planted trap and the reason counterintuitive is set. Argued against the key: with its long tail Velociraptor was about 2 m long, longer than a turkey, but its body mass (about 15 kg) and hip height put it at turkey size, which is how references describe it. volatility: evergreen, a settled fact that cannot change; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: dinosaurs and the film are known worldwide; the answer needs no local knowledge. style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, explanation of 30 words. myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a multiple-choice item. doubts: none on the size. c3 is worded as a comparison of size only, because the film's naming history (Crichton following Gregory Paul) is more tangled than a one-line claim can carry.

evidence.restatement: Velociraptor mongoliensis was roughly turkey-sized: about half a metre tall at the hip and around 15 kg, with a long tail.

claimResults.note: High-risk (checker_doubt): knowledge only in this check. No pinned dataset covers this, and WebSearch was unavailable to this run: the one call attempted was refused because the shared session search limit was already used up, so no search ran. It still needs dataset or web evidence in a confirming check before acceptance (§9.9 rule 3).

evidence.restatement: At that size it was far smaller than an adult human, a horse or a lion.
The Jurassic Park raptors were modelled on larger dromaeosaurids such as Deinonychus and were far bigger than the real Velociraptor.
A Velociraptor forearm bone (ulna) shows quill knobs, the anchor points of wing feathers, so the animal was feathered.
Velociraptor is the animal usually described as turkey-sized: about 2 m from nose to tail tip, around 0.5 m high at the hip, and roughly 15 kg.

claimResults.note: Turkey is the standard museum comparison and the closest option by mass and hip height.

evidence.restatement: Velociraptor was far lighter and lower than an adult human, a horse or a lion.

claimResults.note: True by mass and height. By nose-to-tail length (about 2 m) it is comparable to a person's height, which is the ambiguity noted below.

evidence.restatement: The film raptors were scaled-up versions modelled on the larger Deinonychus, not on real Velociraptor.
A Velociraptor forearm bone (ulna) shows quill knobs, the anchor points for large feathers.

issues.note: 'Size' has no stated measure. Velociraptor matches a turkey in mass and hip height, but its roughly 2 m length matches an adult human's height. Turkey is the conventional comparison and the best fit overall, so the key stands; the editor may prefer 'weighed about as much as' to remove the pedant's route.

editor.reason: Both checks pass, but high-risk claim c1 (key, checker_doubt) rests on knowledge alone in both checks: no pinned dataset covers animal biology and checker A's one search was refused at the session limit, so §9.9 rule 3 cannot pass. No wording fix adds evidence, and stepping down the precision ladder changes claims, so it is cut (§9.2). The content read as sound; redraft it under a new id once evidence can be gathered. For the redraft: B notes that 'size' has no stated measure (a turkey by mass, a human by length), so ask what it weighed about as much as.

stem: The real Velociraptor was about the size of which animal?
